name: Hungary
kernel_parts_used: Schedule (Schedule.flat 15 %: ticks_mono, ticks_convex, ticks_lipschitz, ticks_le_maxRate_mul, ticks_succ, splitting_le_separate instantiated)
Family (perChildByCount proved equal to the § 29/A (2) monthly table: famMonth_kernel; spillAllowance proved equal to the family-allowance spill before the TB cap: fam_spill_kernel)
kernel_gaps: spillAllowance has no cap at the receiving levy: Tbj. § 34 (3) caps the contribution allowance at the TB actually due (and § 34 (6) excludes TB paid only because of a minimum base); written locally (fillOrder over the partners' TB)
a per-child rate table that changes mid-year (Szja § 29/A (2): January-June / July-December 2025): written locally as famMonth2025 / famFrameMonths (Table.perPeriod would need a month-indexed table)
base-reducing allowances applied in a statutory order to different income subsets (§ 29/H; mothers' / under-25 allowances only on wage-type income) and pooled between partners: local
a contribution ceiling counted across income types (Szocho tv. § 2 (2): wages first, then dividends/gains, interest outside): local
self-employed minimum contribution bases (TB on the minimum wage, szocho on 112.5 %) and flat-rate regimes (átalány, KATA): local

headline: Hungary 2025 in Lean (OECD 56/56 lines exact, 45 NAV worked figures exact): the family allowance is proved to act as a 15 %-of-frame credit against tax and TB together (burden = max(0, 33.5 % wage - 15 % frame)); new timing levers around dated starts (mothers of three from October 2025: 478 710 HUF; the 25th-birthday month: 300 000; the 2026 allowance rise: 214 553); the statute's '667 %' is not 1/15 % and NAV's own worked example over-allocates the family allowance.
